problem: The comparison count is wrong. Checking that 5 vertices are pairwise distinct by comparing sequence entries needs 10 comparisons (4+3+2+1), not 5. Comparing only 5 times cannot prove distinctness unless the verifier uses an extra marking array, which is not what the step describes. The total work is therefore 5 edge lookups plus 10 comparisons = 15 operations for n=5.
fix: step 5: Count the work: the verifier makes 5 edge lookups (four consecutive edges plus the closing edge) and up to 10 pairwise comparisons to confirm the 5 vertices are distinct. For n=5, n²=25 and 15 ≤ 25, so the work is of order n², a polynomial (in general n edge lookups and n(n-1)/2 comparisons). answer: The certificate is checked with 5 edge lookups and 10 comparisons, which is within O(n²) time for n=5, so HAMILTONIAN CYCLE is in NP.

problem: "nobody knows whether the two inner containments are strict" can mislead a student into thinking P = NP = PSPACE is still possible. It is known that P ≠ PSPACE (space hierarchy theorem), so at least one of the two containments must be strict; only which one is unknown.
fix: Every P problem is in NP and every NP problem is in PSPACE. Nobody knows whether P = NP or whether NP = PSPACE, but at least one of these two containments is strict, because P ≠ PSPACE is known.
